accent-skill.note: Moved from oklch(0.6 0.15 62) during documentation — 3.7 degrees of hue from status-warn.

display.purpose: The becode wordmark on the empty state. Its only appearance in the product.

headline.purpose: The title of a full surface. At most one per screen region.

title.purpose: The one line a non-engineer must read: the approval question, an error headline, a refusal reason.

body.purpose: Transcript, composer, control labels. The composer's 24px line-height is shared with its highlight mirror and is load-bearing.

label.purpose: Metadata, tool subtitles, sidebar entries, chips. The most-used size in the product.

overline.purpose: Uppercase section marker above a group. Never followed by a rule or border.

code.purpose: Machine strings only: paths, commands, log lines, skill tokens. Never chrome.

shadows.name: observe
shadows.purpose: The observation surface — the pane holding the running target app, and only that. The one element in becode that is not chrome.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Elements that genuinely float free of the layout: dialogs, popovers, the command palette. Never an inline card.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for anything not spring-driven.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric transitions that return to their start.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Sheets and drawers entering from an edge.

motion.name: spring-press
motion.purpose: Tap and press feedback on buttons. Scale to 0.93.

motion.name: spring-swap
motion.purpose: Label and icon slots trading places inside one control.

motion.name: spring-panel
motion.purpose: Overlay panel entrances summoned by pointer.

motion.name: spring-layout
motion.purpose: Shared-layout glides: pills, indicators, panels morphing between positions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animated component checks useReducedMotion and drops to no transform. Non-negotiable.

components.name: Pill Button (Primary)
components.description: The one action the person came to this surface to take. At most one per surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 20px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; user-select: none; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-pill:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 90%, transparent); transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-btn-pill:active { transform: scale(0.93); } .ds-btn-pill:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn-pill:hover, .ds-btn-pill:active { transform: none; } }

components.name: Square Button (Ghost)
components.description: Everything that is not the primary action: toolbar controls, dialog footers, icon actions. No motion.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost"><svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 12a9 9 0 1 0 9-9 9.75 9.75 0 0 0-6.74 2.74L3 8"/><path d="M3 3v5h5"/></svg>Reload</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Composer
components.description: The product's centre of gravity. Hairline at /80 shifting to foreground/25 on focus-within; the textarea's 14px/24px type is shared with the skill-highlight mirror beneath it.
components.html: Make the ticket card less cramped
components.css: .ds-composer { width: 100%; max-width: 520px; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 80%, transparent); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--background); transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-composer:hover { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 25%, transparent); } .ds-composer-text { padding: 6px 8px 0; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.5rem; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-composer-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; min-height: 32px; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-composer-clip, .ds-composer-send { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 9999px; color: var(--muted-foreground); transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-composer-send { margin-left: auto; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); } .ds-composer-clip:hover { background: var(--accent); color: var(--foreground); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: The Status Triple recipe: -600 text (-400 dark), -500/10 fill, -500/30 border. The only element allowed a chromatic fill.
components.html: runningneeds youfailed
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; flex-shrink: 0; margin-right: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-chip-live { color: oklch(0.596 0.145 163.225); background: oklch(0.696 0.17 162.48 / 0.1); border-color: oklch(0.696 0.17 162.48 / 0.3); } .ds-chip-warn { color: oklch(0.666 0.179 58.318); background: oklch(0.769 0.188 70.08 / 0.1); border-color: oklch(0.769 0.188 70.08 / 0.3); } .ds-chip-fail { color: oklch(0.586 0.253 17.585); background: oklch(0.645 0.246 16.439 / 0.1); border-color: oklch(0.645 0.246 16.439 / 0.3); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Hairline border, transparent fill, 8px radius. Error state is carried on the ring, never the border — the unlayered border-color rule in globals.css outranks border utilities.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground); outline: none; transition: box-shadow 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Sidebar Row
components.description: Trailing actions hidden until group-hover, which keeps a two-level tree from reading as a toolbar. A live chat swaps its icon for a 6px Live dot.
components.html: Roomier ticket card
components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; width: 240px; padding: 6px 8px; border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--foreground); transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-row:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 60%, transparent); } .ds-row-dot { flex-shrink: 0; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.696 0.17 162.48); } .ds-row-label { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-row-action { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 8px; color: var(--muted-foreground); opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.15s, background 0.15s; } .ds-row:hover .ds-row-action { opacity: 1; } .ds-row-action:hover { background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); }

components.name: Overline
components.description: 11px uppercase section marker at 0.12em. Never followed by a rule or border — the tracking and the colour are the separation.
components.css: .ds-overline { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground) 70%, transparent); }

components.name: Observation Pane
components.description: The one element in becode carrying a shadow. Holds the running target app; the lift is how the eye knows it is not chrome.
components.css: .ds-observe { width: 100%; max-width: 520px; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 60%, transparent); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--card); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04), 0 8px 24px -8px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.10); overflow: hidden; } .ds-observe-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 60%, transparent); } .ds-observe-url { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-observe-stage { height: 140px; background: var(--background); }

narrative.overview:
becode is a wall of glass around someone else's running product. The person it is built for is not here to read a transcript — they are here to watch a change land in an app they know, and say yes or no to it. So the interface behaves like the frame of a workshop window: it holds the view steady, it labels what is happening on the other side of the glass, and it never asks to be looked at instead. Every surface becode draws is chrome. The content is always something else — the target app, the agent's activity, the diff about to leave the machine.

The material language follows from that. Warm-grey ground, white surfaces, hairline borders at fractional opacity, and a working type range that tops out well below anything the target app will use. Colour is almost entirely absent, and when it appears it is never decoration — it is a fact about state: this is running, this failed, this needs you. The only motion is press physics and layout glides, all of it wired through useReducedMotion, because motion here is feedback on an action, never atmosphere.

Two anti-references are confirmed and binding. becode must not look like an enterprise dashboard — no KPI tile grids, no chart widgets, no sidebar-plus-topbar-plus-breadcrumb scaffolding around a product that has exactly one job. And it must not look like a developer IDE or terminal — no monospace chrome, no syntax-coloured furniture, no file trees. The second is not taste. The person using becode cannot read code, and dressing the tool as a code tool is a lie about who it is for.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-grey ground; chromatic colour reserved entirely for state
Hairline borders at fractional opacity as the primary separator
A working type range of 11–16px, with display type appearing exactly once
Radius that decreases inward: 16px container → 14px panel → 10px row → 8px control
Pill for the one action the person came to take; square for everything else
Reduced-motion honoured on every animated component, without exception

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Chromatic colour appears only when something is true about the system's state. There is no decorative colour in becode, no brand accent on a heading, no coloured illustration. If a hue cannot be traced to a running process, a failure, or a pending decision, it is a defect.

rules.name: The Status Triple Rule
rules.body: A status is always rendered as the same three-part recipe and never improvised: text at the -600 step (-400 in dark), a /10 fill of the -500 step, and a /30 border of the -500 step. Four hues, one recipe, no fifth hue.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are drawn at fractional opacity — border-border/60 is the default, /80 for a surface the person is about to act on, /50 for an inset panel. A border at full strength reads as a table cell, which is the enterprise-dashboard direction.

rules.name: The Machine Strings Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks text that came from or goes to a machine — a path, a command, a log line, a /skill token. It is never used for chrome, labels, headings, or anything a person is meant to read as prose. This is the whole distance between becode and an IDE.

rules.name: The Read-Once Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline appear at most once per surface. Anything that repeats — rows, chips, tool calls, list entries — is Body or smaller. The ceiling exists because the target app is on the other half of the screen and must always win the eye.

rules.name: The Chrome Yields Rule
rules.body: becode's own surfaces never claim more of the viewport than the thing being observed. When a running app, a log tail, or a design system is on screen, it takes the larger share and the chat takes the smaller.

rules.name: The Workshop Window Rule
rules.body: Shadow marks the observation surface. If an element is not the running product and not a true overlay, it is flat — hairline border and a tonal step, nothing else. Adding a shadow to a card, a row, a chip, or a button is a defect.

rules.name: The Nesting Rule
rules.body: Radius decreases inward. A 16px container holds 14px panels, which hold 10px rows, which hold 8px controls. An inner element with a larger radius than its parent is a defect.

rules.name: The One Pill Rule
rules.body: At most one pill per surface. A second pill means two things are claiming to be the primary action, which means neither is.

dos: Do draw every separator as a 1px --border hairline at fractional opacity; /60 is the default, /80 for an actionable surface, /50 when nested.
Do reserve chromatic colour for state, and render it as the Status Triple: -600 text (-400 dark), -500/10 fill, -500/30 border.
Do decrease radius inward — 16px container, 14px panel, 10px row, 8px control.

Do wire every animated component through useReducedMotion, and use the tokens in lib/ease.ts rather than inline curves: SPRING_PRESS for taps, SPRING_LAYOUT for glides, SPRING_PANEL for overlays, EASE_OUT for anything else.
Do put the sentence a person must read at Title (16px) and everything around it at Label (12px) or Body (14px).
Do let the observed thing — the running app, a log tail, a design system — take the larger share of the viewport.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything that is not the observation pane or a true overlay.
Don't use monospace for chrome. It marks machine strings only: paths, commands, log lines, skill tokens.

Don't put a file path, a diff, a stack trace, or a framework name in the primary content of a surface where a decision is made. The person this is built for cannot act on it, and a surface that requires it has failed regardless of correctness.
Don't build KPI tile grids, chart widgets, or breadcrumb-plus-topbar scaffolding. becode has one job.
Don't introduce a fifth status hue, or a chromatic colour with no state behind it.
Don't use Display type anywhere but the empty-state wordmark, or put two pills on one surface.
Don't rely on a border-* utility for error state — the unlayered * { border-color } rule in globals.css outranks it. Carry error on the ring.
